F1 publishes first Social Impact Report; key student scholarship renewed

DM
By David Miller Formula 1 & Motorsport Telemetry Specialist • via Autosport Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Autosport Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Formula 1 has published its first sport-wide Social Impact Report, with over half a million young people across the world having benefited from F1 programmes last year.
  • In initiatives designed to educate, inspire and open pathways into the sport in 2025, youngsters from across 71 countries were able to take a step closer to F1.
  • Official reporting verified via Autosport news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • DAVID MILLER Formula 1 & Motorsport Telemetry Specialist

Aerodynamic Efficiency & Motorsport Racecraft

In premier motorsport disciplines, millisecond gains represent months of high-intensity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) research. The developments reported by Autosport underline how tire degradation curves, ground-effect aero seals, and power-unit energy recovery systems dictate race outcomes. Technical compliance under strict cost caps continues to test team engineering depth.

Big Picture: Upcoming grand prix telemetry and trackside upgrades will reveal which teams hold the definitive technical advantage.

Formula 1 has published its first sport-wide Social Impact Report, with over half a million young people across the world having benefited from F1 programmes last year.

📌 The Core Development

In initiatives designed to educate, inspire and open pathways into the sport in 2025, youngsters from across 71 countries were able to take a step closer to F1.

F1 has also renewed its now-established Engineering Scholarship programme, which was founded in 2021, for three academic years, promising more than £2.4 million in funding. The initiative helps relieve students who would otherwise face key barriers to higher education, including financial and accessibility obstacles. 48 students have already been supported by the programme.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Full tuition fees and living costs will be covered for ten new scholars each year between 2026/27 and 2028/29 at the University of Strathclyde, Imperial College London, the University of Cambridge, the University of Oxford and MUNER in Italy.

For the first time, the contributions of F1, governing body the FIA, all 10 teams and 24 race promoters during the 2025 season have been collated in one report, working to the recommendations of The Hamilton Commission, which was launched by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and the Royal Engineering Academy in 2021.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

• 500,000+ young people given access to the sport through education, STEM and inspiration programmes globally • 100% of Diversity and Inclusion Charter signatories delivering social impact programmes • 1,000+ skills and talent development opportunities spotlighting motorsport and related industries • 29,000+ schools compete annually in the STEM Racing global education initiative • 700+ schools across the UK, South Africa, India and Brazil participated in the British Council’s Learning Sectors education programme • 2,500+ young people participating in activities delivered at Formula 1 events • 50+ wishes granted through Formula 1's partnership with Make-A-Wish • 140 young people attended F1 Academy workshops

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

“Formula 1 has an extraordinary power to inspire, and we want everyone to believe there is a place for them in our sport," said F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali.

"We are turning our commitments into action, working across motorsport to break down barriers and widen access for future generations. We are proud of the progress made and grateful for the collective efforts of Lewis Hamilton, the Hamilton Commission, the FIA, our teams, race promoters, partners and the many organisations helping to create lasting change.
